To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a polymorphism in the gene for TNF-&agr;, an inflammatory cytokine, is associated with worsening of labile anger, but not of depression, during interferon alif therapy.
a single nucleotide polymorphism in the TNF-alpha gene was associated with worsening labile anger, but not with major depressive disorder, during treatment with interferon alpha.
a polymorphism in the TNF-&agr;, but not the 5-HTTLPR, gene is associated with worsening labile anger during interferon alifa therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of mood and anxiety symptoms in patients with chronic hepatitis C who are receiving treatment with interferon alifor the first time.
the role of cytokines in the development of depression and other mood disorders.
the relationship between cytokine genes and mood disorders in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNF-&agr;-308G/A is not associated with depression, and that the TNF-&agr;−308A/G polymorphism is associated with labile anger during interferon alif-based therapy.
TNF-&agr;, a cytokine, may be a factor that influences labile anger, but not major depression, in a subgroup of patients with HCV who are being treated with interferons.
the A308G polymorphism of the TNF-&agr; gene was associated with worsening labile anger during interferon alif therapy, but not with major depressive disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the A allele of the TNF-&agr;-308G polymorphism is associated with increased susceptibility to worsening labile mood symptoms, including anger, during treatment with interferon alifor hepatitis C.

the TNF-&agr;-308G polymorphism was associated with increased labile anger, fatigue, and TNF-&agr;, but not major depressive disorder, during treatment with interferon alifor chronic hepatitis C virus infection.
the TNF-alpha gene polymorphism A308G is associated with labile anger during interferon alpha therapy, but it is not associated with major depression or fatigue.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic variability in tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) is associated with worsening of labile anger during treatment with interferon alif, a cytokine that is also known to increase TNF-α levels.
the genetic variability in the promoter region (rs1800622) of tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is associated with labile anger during interferon alpha treatment.
the TNF-&agr;-308G allele is associated with increased labile anger and fatigue during interferon alif therapy.
